articleTitle: Generative AI for Wireless Interference Modeling: Text-Controlled Waveform Synthesis Using Stable Diffusion
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Modern communication systems face challenges in replicating jammer behaviors when interference parameters are unknown. This study explores the use of Stable Diffusion, fine-tuned with LoRA and DreamBooth, to generate high-level, text-based abstractions that characterize unknown interference patterns. By utilizing a single jammer and receiver, and providing spectrogram images of the received signals, the model is able to generate reasonable representations of the interference. Unlike traditional methods that rely on predefined signal models, our approach enables the synthesis of interference spectrograms without prior knowledge of jammer parameters or transmitted signals. By leveraging diffusion models, we provide a scalable and flexible framework for approximating and representing unknown interference, offering a novel direction for abstracted interference modeling in software-defined radio (SDR) systems.

articleTitle: Design of a Generalized Chebyshev Filter With a Sloped Passband
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel filtering equalizer concept, which enables the design of a desired passband slope while maintaining filtering characteristics. The mathematical equations used to design for a given slope are provided, and the design methodology of the required filtering polynomials is also shown. A third-order lumped-element filtering equalizer with a 3 dB slope along the passband is designed, fabricated, and measured to verify the theory and design methodology. The proposed filter equalizer concept has the potential to both increase the flatness of an overall system response and thus decrease the error vector magnitude (EVM) while also decreasing the cost, size, weight, and power (C-SWaP) of future RF and microwave systems.

articleTitle: A Systematic Design Method Based on Vector Analysis for mmW DCML Divider
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: The traditional RC delay model and the small-signal model do not suffice for a precise analysis of the dynamic current mode logic (DCML) divider in the millimeter-wave (mmW) frequency band. This paper explores the current vector model and examines the prerequisites for the proper functioning of the DCML, including phase, gain, and amplitude aspects, using expressions and vector diagrams as references. To fulfill the frequency division requirements of mmW ultra-wideband phaselocked loops, a broadband DCML4 divider has been designed based on the aforementioned analysis. Simulation results show that with an input power of -4 dBm, the maximum frequency division range for a single sub-band can reach up to 137.5% (from 5 to 27 GHz). The center frequency is adjusted via biasing, enabling the total frequency coverage to achieve 150% (ranging from 5 to 35 GHz). At a supply voltage of 1.2 V, the average power consumption is only 6.72 mW.

articleTitle: Memory Arrays for FMCW Radar Signal Processing:A Feasibility Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper demonstrates that in-memory computing or memory arrays (MA) are feasible for low-latency radar signal processing, which is critical for modern radar applications. For frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radars, this work shows that the operating range (distance) of the radar is limited by the size of the MA and the radar's bandwidth. While larger arrays extend the operating range, parasitics deteriorate the accuracy of the measurement. Further, programming errors at lower conductance values have a greater impact on the accuracy of beat signal estimation and therefore memory devices that exhibit lower error at low conductance will result in better performance in radars. Finally, an architecture for calculating the analytic signal is proposed, and simulations demonstrate reasonable (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 12 \%$</tex>) accuracy for the selected device parameters with nearly instantaneous theoretical latency.

articleTitle: A Study on GaN MMIC Power Amplifier Stability-Performance Design Tradeoffs at X Band
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work presents a measured comparison of two MMIC power amplifiers (PAs) that have nearly the same design except for different degree of on-chip stabilization. In MMIC design, it is often necessary to overdesign stability because of the difficulty of post-fabrication correction, but this comes at the cost of in-band RF performance. As an example of this tradeoff, we compare two different X-band MMIC PAs, one of which is unstable without off-chip capacitance. The less stable design exhibits 0.58 dB higher gain and 3.4 percentage point higher efficiency at the design frequency of 10 GHz.

articleTitle: S-Band Active Circulator with Reactive Load Tuning for Isolation Recovery
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work presents a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.4-\text{GHz}$</tex> gallium nitride (GaN) active circulator with independently tunable reactive loads, which can compensate for impedance mismatch and maintain isolation that results from phased array scan impedance. Simulated results demonstrate isolation improvements of 13.4, 10.5, 19.7 and 31.8 dB for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$|\Gamma|$</tex> mismatches of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.2\left(\theta=180^{\circ}\right.$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left.\theta=270^{\circ}\right)$</tex> and 0.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\theta=0^{\circ}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\theta=90^{\circ})$</tex>, respectively. This concept shows promise for application in full duplex phased array front ends, where high isolation is critical.

articleTitle: Study of Specular and Non-Specular Reflection of Pyramidal Absorber Arrays
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Microwave absorbers are usually designed to minimize specular reflection in a wide range of incident angles. However, new threats in stealth systems, especially multistatic radars, require redefining performance and studying not only specular but also non-specular reflections. Thus, this study focused on pyramidal arrays that could excite non-specular reflections together with absorption. The impact of periodicity and shape on the compromise between non-specular reflections/absorption is especially investigated.

articleTitle: 3D-Printed Reconfigurable Communication System Based on Tunable Liquid Crystals
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents an additively manufactured communication system for V-Band applications using a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2 \times 2$</tex>-antenna array in which each element can be controlled by an individual liquid crystal (LC) based phase shifter. To integrate the anisotropic material into the feed structure, a cavity made of UV-curable photopolymer resin is printed using stereolithography. A targeted beam steering angle of 7° was achieved, while the measured gain of the phased antenna array was between 16.18 dB and 14.02 dB at a center frequency of 62.5 GHz.

articleTitle: A Feature Pyramid Network Based Detection Approach for Multi-Scale Target Detection in Stationary Short-Range Radar
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a deep learning-based Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) for object detection on range-Doppler maps in a stationary short-range radar setup operating at 60 GHz with 4 GHz bandwidth. The FPN model enables multiscale feature extraction, detecting large and small objects in complex, cluttered environments. It offers an alternative to traditional CA- and OS-CFAR detectors combined with DBSCAN, which can struggle with such variations. Holistic image processing through convolutional kernels in a one-stage architecture can help overcome limitations from clutter and noise points by enabling detection and clustering within a single process. Achieving an F1 score of 0.8683 at a 95% confidence threshold, the FPN balances precision (0.9050) and recall (0.8345), demonstrating competitiveness with OS-CFAR (F1: 0.8534) and CA-CFAR (F1: 0.8776). By capturing hierarchical features, the FPN learns contextual patterns beyond fixed-threshold methods, ensuring reliable detection of diverse target dimensions. Its real-time, edge-based data processing capabilities open opportunities for applications in smart homes, industrial automation, and infrastructure management.

articleTitle: Distributed Repeaters for Extending the Range of Passive Harmonic RF Tags
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Passive harmonic radio frequency (RF) tags are favorable for their ability to perform in cluttered environments where access to the tag for battery maintenance is difficult and time consuming. A crucial limitation with passive harmonic RF tags is their range and the large amounts of power that is needed to turn on the nonlinear device that will retransmit the harmonic of the incident signal. In this paper, harmonic RF tag repeaters are introduced to increase the range of the tag while also increasing the power incident on the tag that turns on the nonlinear device that produces the harmonic signal. A 2.4GHz and 4.8-GHz bi-directional repeater is used to amplify the fundamental and harmonic signals between the source and the RF tag. Measured and simulated results indicate that with the inclusion of repeaters, the range of the passive tag is improved more than 3 times from 2-m to at least 6-m with only 1 repeater and the power incident to turn on the nonlinear device is improved with distance.

articleTitle: Highly Efficient MIMO-OFDM Imaging Using Shared Transmission Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This study investigates a novel radar imaging framework utilizing orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) signals to simultaneously achieve high-resolution imaging and efficient bandwidth utilization in a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) configuration. The proposed system employs two transmit and two receive antennas operating at closely spaced carrier frequencies of 2.4 GHz and 2.415 GHz, each occupying an overlapping bandwidth of 400 MHz. By enabling concurrent transmission and reception within the same time and frequency slots, this approach achieves precise crossrange and down-range imaging with minimal interference. A frequency domain image reconstruction technique using backprojection is employed, facilitating accurate spatial representation of objects in simulations. Compared to conventional methods, the presented approach eliminates the need for time-division multiplexing (TDM) or frequency-division multiplexing (FDM), thereby enhancing temporal and spectral efficiency. Simulation results validate the system's ability to generate images of twodimensional objects while maintaining robustness in the presence of spectral and temporal interference.

articleTitle: Enabling Digital Predistortion in High Fractional Bandwidth Cellular Multiband Scenarios with Direct-Sampling and Real-Valued Signals
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: As we increase the fractional bandwidth of a cellular multiband system, at a certain point, the even-order distortion components start to fall inside nearby bands. To enable multiband systems to operate at high fractional bandwidth while still respecting standard requirements with high throughput, one must control these unwanted emissions as well. In this paper, a novel digital predistortion model is presented, capable of canceling both odd- and even-order distortion components. This technique explores the commonly used high-sampling rate RF-DACs/RF-ADCs, but in direct-sampling mode, where up- and down-conversion blocks are bypassed. It processes real-valued signals and the computational complexity is comparable to its complex-valued counterpart, while improving the linearization performance.

articleTitle: A Variable-Power Supply-Modulated Class-E GaN Power Amplifier With 81 % Efficiency Over 10 dB Back-Off for VHF Pulsed Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a drain-modulated class-E GaN PA that exhibits over 81 % drain efficiency over 10 dB output power back-off. The PA employs a square-wave CW drive based on digital ICs and the drain is modulated between 4 and 28 V to produce variable output powers with high efficiency. The PA capacitors and inductors are manually tuned to achieve high back-off efficiency over the bandwidth. The PA achieves an output power of 51 W at 28 V and drain efficiency stays above 81 % for drain voltages above 8 V. Drain modulator losses are minimal with a maximum drop of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.3-0.7 ~\mathrm{W}$</tex> in power and less than about 2 percentage points in efficiency, thanks to the use of an integrated GaN-on-Si half-bridge with only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5-\mathrm{m} \Omega$</tex> onresistance and 2-ns switching speed. These findings make the design a suitable and desirable choice for variable-power pulsed radar applications in the VHF band.

articleTitle: Modeling the Response of a Wireless Harmonic Sensor in a Multi-Layer Environment for Landslide Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a technique for determining the electrical properties of soil by analyzing signal propagation through a stratified medium. The improvement in the extraction of soil permittivity using a model that accounts for internal reflections within the stratified medium is demonstrated. Additionally, the paper utilizes an experimental approach for isolating the forward and reverse transmission paths of a harmonic signal within a soil structure. The work is part of an effort to extract soil property information using a harmonic sensor to develop an electromechanical model for more effective monitoring of potential landslides.

articleTitle: Characterization of Ferromagnetic Resonance Identification (Fmr-Id) Tag in Semi-Wireless Configuration
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work characterizes a ferromagnetic resonance identification (FMR-ID) tag with magnetic nanowires (MNWs) in an anodized aluminum oxide (AAO) template using a semiwireless configuration. The MNWs exhibit distinct ferromagnetic resonance (FMR) frequencies under DC magnetic field variation. A benchmark test using an electromagnet (Emag) to generate a controlled low DC field and vector network analyzer (VNA) operating from 15-30 GHz, produced 5-bit data. To demonstrate portability, Emag is replaced with Disc-shaped permanent magnets (Pmag) that also validate a 5-bit data response. A semiwireless detection setup (a horn antenna and a metamaterial patch antenna (MMPA)) with lower bandwidth successfully retrieved 2bits of the data. Pmag and Emag FMR responses have similar slopes to the Kittel equation with an offset of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1 \text{GHz}$</tex>, believed to be due to DC field differences. These predictable responses demonstrate the feasibility of a semi-wireless FMR-ID system for use in enhanced RFID security applications.

articleTitle: Area-Efficient UWB CMOS Power Amplifier with Hybrid Trifilar
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper designs a wide-band (WB) power amplifier (PA) fabricated in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18 \mu\ \mathrm{m}$</tex> CMOS process. The PA uses three cascaded inductive peaking amplifiers with a resistor in series with an inductor as the amplifier load. The sub-amplifiers use three load-on-chip inductors compacted in the same area to form two pairs of orthogonal transformers to reduce chip area. At 6.5 GHz, the power gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}$</tex> is 19.06 dB; at 8 GHz, the power gain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}$</tex> is 17.18 dB. The fabricated PA with the trifilar occupies an area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.88 \times 0.74\ \text{mm}^{2}$</tex> including the input/output pads. Two design techniques are used in the UWB PA for low die area: (a) a lowcoupling orthogonal transformer, and (b) a coupling transformer in series with resistors. The three inductors form a trifilar with coupling and small coupling coefficients.

articleTitle: State-of-the-Art Load-Pull Simulation Methods for Next-Generation Power Amplifier Design
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Load-pull simulations are crucial in RF and microwave engineering for assessing power amplifier performance. This paper presents advanced test benches for load-pull setups, leveraging Keysight ADS to obtain more efficient and comprehensive data. We introduce an enhanced version of the traditional method with an improved gain compression simulation controller. Additionally, we propose a novel vector network analyzer (VNA)inspired load-pull test bench. This test bench not only provides detailed information about the device under test (DUT) but also serves as a digital twin for VNA-based load-pull measurement setups.

articleTitle: Additively Manufactured Circular Polarized V-Band Phased Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Due to the demand for inter-satellite V-band communication between CubeSats, a circular polarized phased shifted <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times 4$</tex> horn antenna array was designed. The whole structure includes two parts, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times 4$</tex> linear polarized horn antenna array, manufactured with Selective Laser Sintering - Fine Details Resolution (SLS-FDR) technology, and a circular polarizer that was manufactured with Projection Micro Stereolithography (P <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex> SLA). With the help of waveguides of different length, the antenna array could be measured at a phase difference of 120°. They serve as placeholders and are included to be replaced by liquid crystal (LC) phase shifters in later application. The beam steering angle of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1 \times 4$</tex> antenna array reached 10° and 11°. The measured axial ratios (AR) at the two steering angles are 2.84 dB and 3.61 dB.

articleTitle: A 20-32 Ghz Ka-Band MMIC LNA in GaN-on-SiC Designed for a Heterogeneous Integration Process
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a gallium nitride (GaN)-on-SiC Monolithic Microwave Integrated Circuit (MMIC) Low Noise Amplifier (LNA) with high dynamic range and low noise figure in a 150 - nm commercial process for use in a heterogeneous integration package. The two-stage MMIC LNA has a peak linear gain of 15.8 dB and a minimum noise figure of 2.6 dB from 20 to 32 GHz while consuming 300 mW of dc power. The measured 1-dB compression point (P1dB) at 22 GHz is 20 dBm. The effects on simulated performance due to the device selection, matching techniques, and packaging stackup will also be discussed. Finally, we will comment on future plans to test the LNA inside a heterogeneously packaged environment.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a Compact and Broadband On-Chip Modified Three-Conductor Transmission Line Balun at G-Band
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper studies the design and characterization of a millimeter-wave passive planar balun, which is implemented in the back end of line of a high-speed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$130-\text{nm}$</tex> SiGe BiCMOS technology. A modified three-conductor sub-quarter-wavelength transmission line based balun with an additional compensated transmission line is proposed to obtain a broad bandwidth, a compact area and reduced port imbalances. By means of a short termination approach and a deembedding method for reciprocal three-port component, measurement results show a 3-dB bandwidth from 140 GHz to 220 GHz with a minimum insertion loss of 0.7 dB. The amplitude imbalance is less than 0.8 dB and the phase error of differential output signals remains below 4° across the entire bandwidth. To the best knowledge of the authors, this proposed balun consumes the smallest area of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.0038 ~\text{mm}^{2}$</tex> (excluding the pads) with the best phase balance at the G-band.

articleTitle: Coupled Resonator Band-Reject Filters with All Positive Inter-Resonator Couplings
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This work demonstrates the synthesis of band-reject filters comprising cascaded coupled resonator configurations exhibiting all positive inter-resonator couplings. Filters with all positive couplings are easier to manufacture and are less susceptible to temperature & vibration requirements. Several synthesized filter networks are illustrated proving the proposed concept together with the EM implementation of an 8-resonator band-reject filter implemented utilizing coaxial resonators.

articleTitle: OFDM-Based Joint Communication and Ranging with Improved Accuracy Under Signal Bandwidth Constraints by Ideal Sinc Interpolation: Cramer-Rao Lower Bound and 60 GHz Over-the-Air Validation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Joint communication and sensing (JCAS) integrates communication and sensing into the same system. As orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) remains the standard in 5G and beyond, communication-centric JCAS is a critical technology. We propose OFDM-based joint communication and ranging that improves delay estimation accuracy under signal bandwidth constraints for channels with a dominant path, using ideal sinc interpolation achieved by frequency-domain zeropadding. The Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) is derived for the variance of delay estimation in zero-mean additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channels. An over-the-air (OTA) 60 GHz testbed was built with carrier frequency offset (CFO) calibration. We demonstrate sub-ns delay estimation, leading to decimeterlevel ranging accuracy, and the measured standard deviation of repeated delay estimations are shown to approach the CRLB benchmark. The proposed method leverages fast Fourier transform (FFT) for efficient computations and proves effective for well-controlled industrial settings like liquid level detection and structural displacement measurements.

articleTitle: A Novel Filtering Phase Shifter with a 180-Degree Phase Shift Using Switchable Electric/Magnetic Coupling
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a novel filtering phase shifter that utilizes a reconfigurable filter to achieve a 180-degree differential phase shift. The phase shift is electronically controlled by changing the equivalent physical geometry, which enables switching between electric- and magnetic-coupling. The design is verified using a 4.15 GHz bandpass filter made with split-ring resonators. Simulated results show a differential phase shift of 180-degrees with a phase variation span of 11.7-degrees over a 0.5 dB ripple bandwidth of 260 MHz (6.3 % fractional bandwidth) with 1.41 dB of insertion loss.

articleTitle: Additive Manufactured Embedded Ground Plane Design for 3D Heterogeneous Integration and Packaging of RF Chips
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel, fully additivemanufactured approach to 3D heterogeneous integration and packaging of RF chips. The proposed solution utilizes an embedded ground plane to create RF transitions using transmission lines. This technique assists with the fabrication of multi-layer structures in the future. By integrating 3D-printed ground planes into fully additive manufactured processes, more flexible impedance matching has been shown in the packaging of RF chips. Using this aforementioned method, impedance matching at higher layers has been achieved, allowing for the fabrication of more complex 3D-printed layered circuits.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Modeling Single-Layer Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative approach to develop simulation models for single-layer capacitors. Effective simulation models for single-layers capacitors have historically not been widely available. The present work has resulted in broadband, measurement-validated equivalent-circuit and 3D electromagnetic models for single-layer capacitors. These models are validated to frequencies as high as 67 GHz and offer flexibility to allow the designer to adapt the model to a specific use case. In addition, parameters for the bond wire attachment are included, resulting in models with variable application configurations that retain high levels of accuracy.

articleTitle: An Optimizing Method for FMCW Chirp Linearity Based on Continuous Frequency Step Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a method for optimizing chirp linearity in frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) signal sources, utilizing continuous frequency step analysis. The study delves into the connection between the phase-locked loop (PLL) loop bandwidth and the chirp slope. Additionally, it examines how variations in frequency step granularity impact the root mean square (RMS) FM error across three distinct radar operational modes: long-range, medium-range, and short-range. Guided by the proposed optimization model, an FMCW signal source has been designed using a 55 nm CMOS process. This design occupies an area of 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and consuming 178.4 mW of power. The prototype demonstrates a chirp bandwidth of 5.4 GHz and achieves RMS FM errors of 152.7,167, and 201.3 kHz with the chirp slopes of 13.2,22, and 44 MHz/μs, respectively.

articleTitle: Utilizing Information Assets in RF and Microwave Engineering Workflows
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: To meet the demands of next generation wireless communication systems, engineering teams must build flexible, reconfigurable design processes, or workflows, which are able to incorporate and leverage existing information in new ways. The challenge: over the past few decades, Electronic Design Automation (EDA) software platforms have focused on building elaborate user interfaces which obscure the lower-level mechanisms now required to build such workflows. Recently, several vendors have provided access to their EDA toolsets through Application Programming Interfaces (APIs), and in doing so have enabled new possibilities for leveraging information in the engineering design process through automation. This paper studies specific areas in high frequency simulation and measurement where automation can dramatically increase productivity and enable novel solutions to difficult problems by allowing engineering teams to use existing data which was previously inaccessible. Four examples are highlighted: netlist data mining, image-based physical modeling, simulation model extraction from measured data, and improved simulation and measurement speed using AI image completion. Theme: utilizing existing data and streamlining design through automation

articleTitle: Graphene Based Ground Plane for Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Recent studies have demonstrated that graphene films, with three times the thermal conductivity of copper, serve as effective lateral heat spreaders for RF electronics while simultaneously functioning as ground planes to support signal propagation. Patch antennas, particularly those used in remote mobile applications, are known to generate significant heat during operation, necessitating efficient passive thermal management solutions. In this study, we investigate the feasibility of employing reduced graphene oxide (rGO) films as ground planes for patch antennas, leveraging their superior thermal conductivity while maintaining RF performance. We designed and simulated a patch antenna with both copper and rGO ground planes, evaluating their S-parameter performance and benchmarking their radiation characteristics. Experimental measurements of return loss revealed that the rGO-backed patch antenna exhibited additional loss at the resonant frequency compared to its copper counterpart. Additionally, analysis conducted in an anechoic chamber confirmed that the rGO-backed antenna preserved the expected radiation pattern. These findings suggest that rGO ground planes can provide effective thermal management while maintaining RF integrity, making them a promising alternative to copper for next-generation wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Circular Antenna Array for Rotationally Invariant and Bidirectional Transmission in the Near-Field
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this paper, a concept for a monostatic antenna array for rotation invariant transmission in the near-field is presented. The rotational invariance of the antenna is realized by a circular array, whereby the antenna elements are fed in a radial or tangential direction around a common rotation axis. By feeding each antenna element orthogonally, the concept can be extended to a monostatic antenna, which allows it to be used in applications for wireless full-duplex data transmission. The concept is evaluated using 3D electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: A 150-168 GHz Mixer and Quadrupler Unit in SiGe BiCMOS Technology for JCAS Applications Based on DDS Signal Generation Up to 5 GHz
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a fully integrated mixer and quadrupler unit with a 3 dB bandwidth from 150 to 168 GHz and a maximum output power of -15 dBm. The circuit is designed for JCAS applications focusing on the up-conversion of arbitrary ramp sequences (e.g., for FMCW radar) generated by a commercial DDS block. The unit comprises a polyphase filter, LO buffer amplifiers, a double-balanced single-sideband mixer, and a subsequent frequency quadrupler, which provides a bandwidth extension by a factor of four. Thus, 18 GHz of bandwidth in the D-band can be achieved by using a 4.5 GHz DDS signal source. The proposed arrangement is optimized for low phase noise, high spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR), and compatibility with various communication applications. An SFDR exceeding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2 4 d B c}$</tex> is maintained across the entire measured RF frequency range (150 to 168 GHz), with suppression of spurs greater than 30 dBc observed in the 156 to 164 GHz range. The circuit was fabricated using a 90 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f_{\mathrm{t}} / f_{\text{max }}$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$300 \text{GHz} / 500 \text{GHz}$</tex>, respectively, and has a power consumption of 175 mW.

articleTitle: A Reconfigurable Polarization Patch Antenna Array with Beam Steering for CBRS MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel patch antenna array designed for the Citizens Broadband Radio Service (CBRS), specifically targeting the 5G New Radio (NR) n48 band. The antenna operates within a frequency range of 3.58 GHz to 3.66 GHz and demonstrates both beam-steering capabilities and polarization agility. A diagonal feed placement on the square patch plays a pivotal role in achieving these functionalities without altering the antenna aperture, representing a significant advancement in patch antenna design. Beam steering and polarization switching are accomplished solely by adjusting the relative phase of each antenna port. This antenna array can switch between linear (horizontal and vertical) and circular (left-hand and right-hand circular polarization) which is highly desirable in CBRS MIMO application. This array exhibits an axial ratio of less than 0.1 dB across the entire operational bandwidth, indicating excellent circular polarization performance. This innovative approach simplifies the design process while enhancing versatility. The compact design and multifunctional capability make this antenna a promising candidate for 5G communication systems.

articleTitle: UWB UHF Dual-Polarized Dipole Antenna with Low-Profile Microstrip Balun
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: We present design and implementation results of a UHF (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$600-900 \text{MHz}$</tex>) antenna array for a high-power radar ice sounder followed by an improved array design concept. Results for a 64-element airborne array and a 16-element ground-based array are reported. Each antenna element consists of dualpolarized microstrip dipoles and aperture-coupled microstrip baluns that are soldered perpendicular to the dipole. Third order lumped-element impedance matching networks are used to increase the bandwidth. The operational bandwidth of the airborne array is limited to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$675-725 \text{MHz}$</tex>, due in part to impedance mismatches from balun design, non-ideal element and ground plane separation, and mutual coupling. To address the electrical mismatch and integration challenges of the initial implementation, we present a revised antenna design with a nearplanar microstrip balun network. The total height of the antenna is reduced by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 57 \%$</tex>. Full-wave simulations show an improved return loss at the higher end of the bandwidth, and an increase in average nadir gain by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 1 ~\text{dB}$</tex> for both airborne and ground-based configurations.

articleTitle: Low-Power Wireless Multi-Channel Surface Electromyography Sensor for Facial Muscle Sensing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: Today's electromyography (EMG) sensor systems usually require complicated setups for data acquisition and processing. Especially for facial muscle sensing, small and portable systems are required to allow longer and more realistic measurements. Research in the area of affective states and distinct emotions requires larger studies with extended recording times. Therefore, the acceptance of the sensor by the subjects is crucial. In collaboration with a team of clinical psychologists, this work presents a Bluetooth Low Energy 5.4 enabled wireless surface EMG sensor with edge pre-processing and post-processing on a PC for data evaluation.

articleTitle: Low-Profile Meandering Spiral Antenna Using an Absorber-Loaded EBG Cavity
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a meandering spiral antenna (MSA) with a compact absorber-loaded electromagnetic band gap (EBG) cavity. The novel EBG structure features unit cells that are implemented using two substrates connected with vias through an air gap. Inserted in the air gap is a thin layer of RF-absorbing foam utilized to improve the axial ratio bandwidth compared to an absorber-less EBG structure. The design utilized the EBG to achieve a very low cavity height of 12.8 mm which is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.16 \lambda$</tex> at the lowest operating frequency of 3.8 GHz. Despite this compact size, the antenna maintains key performance parameters including a reflection coefficient below -10 dB from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.0-8.0 \text{GHz}$</tex>, RHCP gain exceeding 0 dBic from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.0-7.9 \text{GHz}$</tex> (peaking at 4.8 dBic), and an axial ratio below 3 dB from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3.8-6.6 \text{GHz}$</tex>. The proposed design, which combines size reductions from the MSA and hybrid EBG structure, is an innovative solution for broadband spaceconstrained antenna systems.

articleTitle: Power-Efficient Single-Input Star Outphasing Amplifier with Large Output Backoff: Invited Paper
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: A new three-transistor outphasing power amplifier (OPA) with a star topology is presented. It features two output backoff (OBO) power levels like the three-transistor Doherty PA but achieves a flatter high efficiency between peak and its 9.54 dB OBO. A low-power two-transistor RF outphasing driver for generating the three required input RF signals from a single RF input is also proposed for driving the Star OPA.

articleTitle: Delayed Crosstalk Digital Predistorter for MIMO Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In modern wireless communication systems, multiinput multi-output (MIMO) technology has been pivotal in achieving high data rates and enhanced spectral efficiency. However, the nonlinear behavior of Power Amplifiers (PAs) in MIMO systems can significantly degrade system performance. This paper proposes a novel delayed crosstalk digital predistorter (DC-DPD) model for (MIMO) radio systems. The proposed model demonstrates that incorporating delayed crosstalk improves the performance of the digital predistorter. The model was subjected to experimental validation utilizing an Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexing (OFDM) signal with a bandwidth of 50 MHz and employing 64-QAM modulation using the same model with and without the delayed crosstalk. Experimental results show that the DC-DPD model outperforms by up to 3 dB the 2D memory cubic spline basis (MCSB) model DPD of Normalized Mean Square Error (NMSE) and Adjacent Channel Power Ratio (ACPR).

articleTitle: Exploiting Non-Uniform Quantization for Enhanced Ilc in Wideband Digital Pre-Distortion
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this paper, it is identified that lowering the reference level at the vector signal analyzer can significantly improve the performance of iterative learning control (ILC). We present a mathematical explanation for this phenomenon, where the signals experience logarithmic transform prior to analogue-to-digital conversion, resulting in non-uniform quantization. This process reduces the quantization noise of low-amplitude signals that constitute a substantial portion of orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) signals, thereby improving ILC performance. Measurement results show that compared to setting the reference level to the peak amplitude, lowering the reference level achieves 3 dB improvement on error vector magnitude (EVM) and 15 dB improvement on normalized mean square error (NMSE) for 320 MHz WiFi OFDM signals.

articleTitle: Vensar Reflectarray Rf Modeling and Optimization for the Envision Mission
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper describes the RF modeling and optimization of the reflectarray antenna for the Venus Synthetic Aperture Radar (VenSAR) instrument. VenSAR is a dualpolarized radar operating at S-band (3.2 GHz). The antenna will be employed to perform scientific studies of the surface of Venus. The reflectarray is illuminated by a feed, which is composed of two horns to generate dual polarization (horizontal and vertical). The reflectarray was optimized for beamwidth, side-lobe level, and directivity using the QUPES tool of TICRA. The RF model includes the impact of the spacecraft deck on which the reflectarray antenna is mounted. A performance comparison is made between the reflectarray operating in ideal conditions (no scattering) and the case when the top deck of the spacecraft is included in the analysis.

articleTitle: Hiercharge: Low-Complexity Hierarchical Optimization for Scalable IoT Energy Solution
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper proposes HierCharge, a hierarchical optimization system for scalable Internet-of-Things(IoT) energy solutions using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) equipped with wireless power transmitters. The system is designed to schedule, assign, and execute charging tasks for IoT devices with low computational complexity while minimizing failures and optimizing energy efficiency. Numerical results demonstrate that HierCharge outperforms state-of-the-art AI-based approaches, including Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) and Q-learning, which struggle to converge due to the large system state and complex action space. The proposed method minimizes failures with low computational cost, which makes it a practical and scalable solution for realtime IoT energy optimization.

articleTitle: Wideband Single-Input Load-Modulated Double Balanced Amplifier With Intrinsic Load Insensitivity
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents the first-ever wideband loadmodulated double balanced amplifier (LMDBA) with an intrinsic isolation to load. Building upon the foundational concept of the generic load modulated balanced amplifier (LMBA), by setting the control amplifier (CA) to balanced topology, the LMDBA can inherit the load-mismatch tolerance characteristic of balanced amplifiers, eliminating the need for a magnetic circulator. To demonstrate the principle, a wideband RF-input LMDBA is developed using GaN devices and commercial branchline quadrature hybrid couplers from 1.9-2.7 GHz. The experimental results exhibit an efficiency of 54-75 % at peak power and 45-60 % at 10-dB output back-off (OBO) under the matched condition of load across the band. An efficiency up to 70.2 % at peak power and up to 54.2 % at 10-dB OBO are measured under 2:1 VSWR of load. Additionally, the PA's linearity profiles (AMAM and AMPM) can be well maintained against load mismatch compared to matched condition without reconfiguration. In modulated measurement, the efficiency and linearity performance can well maintained under various load as well.

articleTitle: W-Band Power Amplifier With Reconfigurable Output Matching Network
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents an on-chip load-reconfigurable three-stage MMIC power amplifier (PA) in a 40-nm GaN process. A staging ratio of 1: 2: 4 is used for two drive stages and an output reactively power-combined stage. The output part of the matching network following the combiner is a discrete reconfigurable impedance matching network that uses two shunt <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4 \times 37.5 \mu\ \mathrm{m}$</tex> HEMTs. The tunability is achieved by changing the gate bias voltage of the devices between 3 states. The reconfigurable network enhances efficiency and output power of the PA as the load impedance is varied from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\vert\Gamma\vert=[0-0.8]$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\angle \Gamma$</tex> from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$[0-360^{\circ}]$</tex>. The PA small-signal measurements show a peak gain of 18.1 dB at 77 GHz. For an input power of 11 dBm, the output power is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25\ \text{dBm}(0.3\ \mathrm{W}$</tex>), with a large-signal gain of 13 dB and power-added efficiency of 10 % at 77.2 GHz.

articleTitle: An Intermodulation Distortion Suppression Selfinjecting Real-Time RF Signal Processing Feedback Loop
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to suppress third order intermodulation (IMD3) products by designing a real-time RF signal processing second harmonic self-injection feedback loop. Harmonic separation network and RF signal processing network form a second harmonic self-injection feedback loop in RF active device circuit to cancel out IMD product. To verify the proposed design concept, a prototype is designed, fabricated, and validated both in simulation and measurement. The measurement results align well with circuit EM simulation to demonstrate propose design approach.

articleTitle: Digital Self-Interference Cancellation in Wideband Star Radio Using an Auxiliary Receiver
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a novel digital self-interference cancellation (DSIC) technique in full-duplex radios supporting simultaneous transmission and reception (STAR). Key to the design approach is the development of a behavioral model of the full-duplex radio front-end at the digital baseband. An auxiliary receiver (RX) chain is deployed to capture the transmitter (TX) chain and the leakage channel response. The leaked signal is digitally reconstructed and analog cancellation is performed at the low-noise amplifier (LNA) input to prevent desensitization. The cancellation algorithm is developed on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$16-\text{nm}$</tex> AMDXilinx radio frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) incorporating gigasample speed data converters and field programmable gate array (FPGA) on the same chip. The architecture is directly implemented on the programmable logic (PL) and the model coefficients are calculated offline in the ARM processor of the SoC. The hardware demonstration employs a reduced number of off-the-shelf analog components that provide an impressive digital cancellation of 20 dB for a maximum modulation bandwidth of 400 MHz.

articleTitle: A Novel Integrated Power Detection Circuit for Low Noise Amplifiers in Cellular Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: A novel power sensing method, integrated in low noise amplifier architectures is presented and demonstrated in 130 nm SiGe BiCMOS technology. The power sensor architecture can be utilized to detect blocking signals by supply current variations caused from different amplifier saturation states. Therefore the combined amplifier/power sensor architecture overcomes the need of additional components in the RF signal path for input power sensing. Two sensor architectures are compared while one is implemented. The architectures ability to indicate input power by amplifier saturation is proven by measurement. It is shown that the sensor gives direct feedback at early stages before the amplifier is in full saturation. The amplifier achieves a maximum gain of 14.31 dB and is optimized for the 5G low-band frequency range from 600 MHz to 1 GHz.

articleTitle: A CMOS LNA with Improved Multi-Path Noise-Canceling for K-Band Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents a transformer-based improved multi-path noise-canceling (IMNC) low noise amplifier (LNA) for K-band satellite communications. The design enhances the dual-path noise cancellation and significantly reduces the noise figure. The proposed LNA employs a three-coil transformer with dual-eight-shaped inductor to boost gain, and introduces a noise cancellation path for the common-gate transistor to optimizes noise performance. During the circuit design phase, a multicomponent integrated modeling (MIM) technique is applied, which accurately characterizes the EM field of the LNA and ensures high consistency between simulation and measurement results. The LNA, fabricated in a 40 nm CMOS process, consumes 28.8 mW of power and achieves a peak gain of 12.6 dB. Its 3-dB bandwidth ranges from 19.9 to 25 GHz with a minimum noise figure of 2 dB. The core area of the LNA is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.16 ~\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>.

articleTitle: 5G Filtering Architecture for Handset Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: The rapid growth in mobile wireless communication systems has created an accelerating demand for new RF spectrum bands and new technologies. Furthermore, the increasing functionalities in the limited space of mobile wireless devices demand innovative RF front end (RFFE) architectures. In this work, a state-of-the-art system on chip (SoC) filtering architecture is designed to fulfil the needs of the expanding wireless spectrum in the 5 G sub- 7 GHz (FR1) bands. The system is designed to support uplink and downlink capabilities for both n79 and n77 bands. The module includes active and passive devices, but the scope of this paper is to illustrate the novel filtering architecture. The SoC presented in this paper enhances radio frequency (RF) filter technology to help reduce system interference, increase RF range, and improve transmitter and receiver capabilities.

articleTitle: A Compact 5.6GHz BAW Filter Design Using Meandered Path
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: In this study, we investigate the design of a 5.6GHz BAW filter, demonstrating how modifying the die layout can achieve a 45% reduction in size while maintaining nearly identical performance. A comparison of simulation results and measurement data reveals that the new die layout introduces only a slight increase in insertion loss (less than 0.12 dB) within the band, while exhibiting similar performance in terms of out-of-band characteristics, rejection levels, steepness, and return losses. These findings highlight the trade-off between size reduction and minimal performance loss, making the modified die layout a promising option for compact 5.6GHz filter designs.

articleTitle: Sub-THz MIMO Hybrid Beamforming: D-Band Dual-Channel Analog Beamforming Front-Ends Prototyping
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of novel dual-channel (MIMO hybrid) beamforming wireless front-ends operating in the D-band (sub-THz range), optimized within the 150 to 170 GHz frequency spectrum. The development incorporates analog beamforming networks realized through two 16×16 microstrip Rotman microwave lenses and dual sets of 1-to-16 RF MMIC switches, in conjunction with a 16×2 antenna array comprised of low-profile on-silicon patch antenna elements and a PTFE elliptically extruded dielectric lens. The resulting architecture produces 32 distinct RF beams bifurcated into two sets of 16 beams, each oriented at two elevation angles. Each set is characterized by beams spaced 4 degrees apart in azimuth, collectively resulting in a 64-degree azimuthal scanning capability. Furthermore, the transmit front end is outfitted with 32 parallelized power amplifiers distributed across 8 InGaAs MMIC chips, equipping it to yield approximately 50 dBm effective isotropic radiated power (EIRP). In parallel, the receive front end comprises 32 low-noise amplifiers (LNAs) similarly arrayed across 8 InGaAs MMIC chips, each delivering an active gain exceeding 30 dB, which augments the overall passive antenna array gain of 25 dBi.

articleTitle: Growing into an Adaptive and Reconfigurable Paradigm for Spectrum Sharing
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE Wireless and Microwave Technology Conference (WAMICON)
abstract: A significant movement from rigid use of the wireless spectrum toward adaptive and reconfigurable spectrum use has been prompted by increasing spectral crowding. Some bands have moved to an adaptive sharing model, and proposals are growing for this approach to be applied to additional bands. The process of moving from a fixed, rigid spectrum paradigm to adaptive and reconfigurable use involves maturation of policy and technology at multiple levels within the system of systems. Using the concept of Bloom's Taxonomy from the education discipline, this paper examines the development of a policy and technology progression toward a mature, adaptive and reconfigurable paradigm.
